idiom_name: function type or call signature as the callback contract; util.callbackify/promisify bridges
implementation_notes: TypeScript gives the callback parameter a precise contract with function types ((err: Error | null, data?: Buffer) => void), optional callbacks and overloads for the different completion shapes, while strictFunctionTypes enforces contravariant parameter checking for function-typed properties (method syntax stays bivariant). Node's util.callbackify adapts an async function to an error-first callback API and util.promisify goes the other way, so a callback boundary and a promise boundary can be bridged without rewriting call sites. A named interface with a call signature is justified for overloaded or this-typed callback contracts, or when the name itself documents the API; otherwise inline function types are the native form.
pitfalls: A loosely typed callback (cb: Function) erases the error/result contract; model completion as a discriminated union or overloads so strict mode can catch a missing error argument.
strictFunctionTypes only checks function-typed members, not method declarations - a callback declared with method syntax stays bivariant and accepts unsound handlers.
Passing a method as a callback loses this at run time; declare a this parameter or wrap the reference in an arrow function.
The type system cannot express 'called exactly once', so an implementation that completes twice or never still compiles - guard the terminal call explicitly.
